items.why: 'Agree' khud ek verb hai, isse pehle am/is/are nahi lagta.
'Discuss' ke baad 'about' nahi aata, kyunki discuss ka matlab hi 'baat karna kisi cheez ke baare mein' hai.
'Know' state verb hai; iska -ing form (am knowing) nahi banta.
He/She/It ke saath doesn't aata hai, don't nahi.
'Have' jab 'rakhna/hona' ke matlab mein ho to -ing nahi lagta. Doubt ho to bas 'I have a doubt'.
Sambandh/maalkiyat ke liye simple present: has/have.

items.wrong: He is more taller than me.
items.why: Tall ka comparative 'taller' hai; 'more' aur '-er' ek saath nahi.
Better khud comparative hai; 'more' mat lagao.
Umar batane ke liye 'I am ... years old' bolte hain, 'have' nahi.
Natural tareeka: I am 20 (years old).
'Good name' English mein nahi bolte; seedha 'What is your name?'
Stay = kuch der rukna (hotel). Permanent ghar ke liye 'live'.
'Do the needful' purani Indian office English hai; modern English mein clear sentence likho.

items.wrong: I will revert back to you.
items.right: I will get back to you.
items.why: 'Revert' ka matlab hi 'wapas' hai, aur English mein iska matlab 'purani halat mein jaana' hai. 'Get back to you' sahi hai.
Repeat ke andar hi 'dobara' hai, 'again' double ho jata hai.
Return mein 'back' ka matlab pehle se hai.

items.right: He explained the topic to me.
items.why: Explain ke baad 'to + person' aata hai.

items.wrong: She told to me a story.
items.why: Tell ke baad seedha person: told me.
'Say' ke baad person nahi aata; 'tell' ke baad aata hai.

items.right: I have been waiting since morning.
items.why: 'Since' ke saath present perfect continuous: have been waiting.
'Since' ke saath present perfect, simple present continuous nahi.
Bite hue samay (yesterday) ke saath simple past: saw.

items.wrong: Yesterday I have gone to the market.
items.right: Yesterday I went to the market.
items.why: Past time ke saath simple past.
Did ke baad verb ka pehla form: go.
'Did' ke baad 'go' aata hai, 'went' nahi.
She/He/It ke saath does not.
He/She/It ke saath verb mein -s/-es lagta hai.
They/We/You ke saath 'are'.
'I' ke saath hamesha 'am'.
Plural ke saath 'there are'.
Information gina nahi jata (uncountable): informations galat hai.
Advice uncountable hai, 'advices' nahi.
Furniture uncountable hai.

items.wrong: He gave me a good news.
items.why: News uncountable hai; 'a news' nahi.

items.wrong: I have a lot of works.
items.right: I have a lot of work.
items.why: Work (kaam) uncountable hai.

items.wrong: I want to discuss about this.
items.why: Discuss ke baad 'about' nahi aata.
Know ke saath continuous form nahi.
Understand ke saath -ing nahi lagta.
Like state-verb hai; simple present use karo.

items.wrong: He is a student of class ten.
items.why: Natural tareeka: in class ten.
Kisi cheez mein achha hona = good at.
Weak at / bad at.
Interested ke baad 'in + -ing'.
Fond ke baad 'of'.
Afraid ke baad 'of'.
Agree = verb, 'with' ke saath.
Reach ke baad 'to' nahi aata.
Jaana/aana = to; 'in' andar hone ke liye.
Married ke saath 'to'.
Home ke pehle 'to' nahi lagta.
Enter ke baad 'into' nahi.

items.wrong: My friend is coming from long time.
items.right: My friend has been coming for a long time.
items.why: Kitne samay se = for ya since, with present perfect.

items.right: It has been raining since morning.
items.why: Since ke saath present perfect continuous.
Tell ke baad direct person.
Light jalane ke liye 'switch on' / 'turn on'.
Band karne ke liye 'switch off' / 'turn off'.
Cousin mein hi bhai/behen aa gaya.
Natural: I graduated in 2023 / I have a degree.
Natural question: What time is it?
Sleep = noun/verb; feeling ke saath adjective: sleepy.
Hair uncountable.

items.wrong: He is elder than me by two years.
items.right: He is two years older than me.
items.why: Comparison mein 'older' use karo; elder sirf family mein.

items.right: She is a friend of mine.
items.why: 'My one friend' unnatural hai.
Every ke baad singular noun aur singular verb.
Both = plural.
'Who all' Hindi 'kaun kaun' ka direct anuvaad hai; 'who' kaafi hai.
